findings.title: Native user task prompt is not bound to the accepted frontend deployment
findings.evidence: _transcript requires four roles and then validates only first assistant/toolResult/final assistant. It never reads messages[0] beyond its role. _load_configs normalizes process configs but never opens the bound frontend deployment or its assets.task_prompt FileBinding. A session with a different user prompt, a matching newly derived usage checkpoint/gate session hash, and every other accepted input unchanged returns PASS.
findings.impact: The pure acceptor can label a synthetic case VERIFIED_SYNTHETIC_COMBINATION without proving that native Prime received the root-sealed task prompt. This violates the contract requirement that no unexpected messages pass and leaves task-to-session lineage dependent on the same root driver it is meant to check. It does not expose data or execute anything, but blocks use as independent combination admission evidence.
recommended_fix: Open synthetic.deployment_path through its deployment_identity hash/size/mtime and parse the exact controller deployment without running a producer.

Reopen assets.task_prompt using its exact FileBinding and bound cap, decode strict UTF-8, and require the sole user message content exactly equals [{type:text,text:<opened prompt>}], with no extra content/image.
Because normal/synthetic configs must differ only in frontend identity, require the same deployment identity/path for both or otherwise compare both task prompt bindings.
Add a failing-first wrong-user-prompt case that keeps session/gate/usage hashes internally consistent and expects TOOL_TRANSCRIPT_INVALID.
